On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.” Continue reading...

item.title: Review: Contraceptive pill usage in Great Britain fell drastically in last decade, research finds
item.description: Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth national survey of sexual attitudes and lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception. item.title: Review: Rescuers blocked from a fire. A child killed on the way to school. Miles-long trains are upending US lives
item.description: Communities say big railroad companies won’t act and that lawmakers moving too slowly to address a major problem The drive from the Lockland fire station to a house fire on Patterson Avenue should have taken no more than 45 seconds . But East Wyoming Avenue and Davis Street were both blocked: a Norfolk Southern train was stopped across several streets – the fire engine had to turn around and take a detour via a nearby highway. By the time firefighters snaked through the highway traffic and reached the fire last month, seven minutes after the call came in, 89-year-old Marian Haefner was dead in her own home . item.title: Review: MP hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
item.description: Five helipads built to ferry in VIP guests to wedding hosted by MP Anant Singh, with spectators climbing electricity pylons to catch glimpse of celebrations About 400,000 guests have attended a wedding hosted by a politician in India’s poorest state, choking roads and sending spectators scrambling up electricity pylons for a glimpse of the lavish celebrations. Anant Singh, a six-time MP who is facing dozens of criminal cases including murder charges, invited villagers, political allies and VIPs to his daughter’s wedding in the eastern state of Bihar on Wednesday. Singh denies any wrongdoing regarding the charges he faces. Continue reading...
